title: Spatial N-glycan imaging and XGBoost classify hepatocellular carcinoma tissue
summary: MALDI mass spectrometry imaging of N-glycans was done on tissue sections from two cohorts (discovery n=88, validation n=60), and an XGBoost classifier was trained on 90 glycan features. Pixel-level AUCs were 0.95 (cross-validation) and 0.89 (external validation); biopsy-level AUCs were 1.0 and 0.97, identifying 97% of tumour-containing biopsies. Glutamine synthetase (GS) status was discriminated with an AUC of 0.75 (GS+ n=45, GS- n=17). The study is retrospective and the GS result is modest.
ai_technology: XGBoost classifier on 90 N-glycan imaging features

evidence.tested: Independent validation cohort (n=60) after training on a discovery cohort (n=88); biopsy AUC 0.97.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; small GS subgroups; clinical use untested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost classified tumour versus non-tumour regions and GS status from spatial glycan signals.
